meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone talk to him first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. Kids write in one place and paste into another. And you still haven't said whether anyone heard Owen before that zero went in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays out of his classroom. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A wrong scene number is a citation error, not proof of anything. Is that line anywhere in the play, Hale?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. So what exactly are you proposing for Owen?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, that's what outlines are for. And you still haven't put anything on the table.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

Then Owen does the rewrite, to put this behind him, and that is the only reason. Private, a date before December 1, and the promise that nothing touches his record, in your email tonight. The outline point stays open, and it goes in mine.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
He works after school some days; I'll check his shift tonight and confirm. Put Thursday the twelfth in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay after school on Thursday, November 12, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in his record. I still want that promise in writing, and I want the outline point answered properly rather than counted against him. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, and she still wants your written promise tonight that nothing goes on his record; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you got there well before her call.
What moved her: You turned the screen to show the version history with its exact late-night times and answered her pasting defence by inviting a dated draft, which gave her something she could check rather than an opinion.
What cost ground: You never answered whether Owen was spoken to before the zero went in, so she kept a procedural grievance open the whole meeting.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after your apology, when she asked whether Owen was heard first, answer that one question directly before showing any evidence.
